assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped how economists and policymakers understand technology, task content, and trade exposure as drivers of labour demand, wage polarisation and local labour-market adjustment. The task framework and the China-shock evidence changed both theory and empirical practice, and the policy relevance is large.
assessment.attribution: Katz is central to the skill-premium and education-versus-technology literature, Autor to the task approach and the trade-shock work, and Hanson to the local labour-market adjustment evidence. Dorn is an important co-author but more junior in credit. A three-person prize is coherent, though the choice of Hanson over Dorn is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: The work spans about three decades. The skill-biased change and task literature is well established, and the China-shock findings have been replicated and extended.
uncertainties: Debate over the magnitude and persistence of the China-shock effects and over identification with shift-share instruments.
How to weigh Dorn against Hanson.
Overlap of Katz with the mobility candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade framework changed how the gains from trade are analysed, bringing selection, productivity reallocation and the extensive margin into the core model. It also shaped the later empirical and quantitative trade literature.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear originating contribution, and Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exporting versus FDI. Redding is a major contributor on quantitative and spatial extensions but is a later contributor to the core idea.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation and extension. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, so the timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether Redding or other contributors such as Bernard and Jensen deserve inclusion.
Helpman's separate claim through the political-economy-of-trade candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built a systematic theoretical and empirical framework linking electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal outcomes. It brought political institutions into mainstream modelling of economic policy and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the core authors of the constitutional and electoral-rules programme. Besley is central on state capacity and accountability, so the three-person grouping is natural.
assessment.maturity: The work has been mature since the 2000s, with extensive empirical follow-up.
uncertainties: Recent recognition of institutions research may reduce the case for near-term timing.
Identification in the cross-country constitutional evidence is weaker than in the micro-level work.
Committee-member connections are disclosed but not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, microfounded pricing and rule-based monetary policy, underpins modern central-bank analysis and has had a large practical impact on policy practice.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse across many contributors. Calvo's pricing model, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's synthesis are the most separable pillars. Gali, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum have strong claims too, so any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature after more than three decades, with the framework embedded in policy institutions.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution makes the three-person limit awkward.
Some of the framework's performance during and after the 2008 crisis and the post-2020 inflation has been criticised.
Partial overlap with the 2022 macro-finance recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Used population-scale administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run effects of policies and teachers. This changed the empirical standard for studying opportunity and linked it directly to policy design.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the programme. Hendren is central to the neighbourhood and causal-place-effects work, and Friedman to the teacher value-added and mobility studies. Katz is a key collaborator on Moving to Opportunity and is also credited in another candidate.
assessment.maturity: The major results are from roughly 2014 onward. They are influential, but long-run replication and external validity are still developing.
uncertainties: Relatively young body of work for a prize.
Debates on interpreting place effects and on teacher value-added validity.
Overlap with Chetty's public-economics candidacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Re-established long-run top-income and wealth data as a central empirical object, with large effects on scholarly agenda and public debate on distribution and taxation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the founders of the top-incomes series, and Zucman is central to offshore wealth and distributional national accounts. The credit is well defined.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of influence. The data have been widely adopted but also contested.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the income and wealth-allocation estimates.
The conceptual theory of capital accumulation is contested.
Part of the contribution is data construction rather than identification of mechanisms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Diagnosed the weak-instrument problem and developed identification-robust inference, which directly improves the reliability of instrumental-variable evidence across applied fields, including labour and education.
assessment.attribution: Staiger and Stock (1997) established the weak-instrument problem, and Andrews contributed foundational robust-test theory. Moreira (conditional likelihood ratio test) and Yogo are also important, so the three-name selection is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: The literature has had about three decades of development and is now standard practice, for example in first-stage F-statistic diagnostics.
uncertainties: Credit is split between diagnosis and solution.
The methodological impact is broad but less visible than a substantive discovery.
Stock's competing credit in forecasting methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are among the most widely used tools in applied microeconomics and macroeconomics, making it possible to estimate dynamic relationships with panel data under unobserved heterogeneity.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond (1991) and Arellano-Bover and Blundell-Bond are the core contributions. Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen, and Hansen's GMM are important antecedents, and some are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with more than thirty years of use. Known issues such as instrument proliferation and weak instruments are well documented.
uncertainties: Incremental relative to the Hansen GMM foundation.
Possible misuse in applied work.
Blundell's overlap with the structural labour candidate.
